paper_title: A Proof of Shur’s Conjecture on the Growth of Power-Free Languages over Large Alphabets
classifications: Mathematics of computing → Combinatorics on words
statement: On the other hand, as conjectured by Shur, and later by the second author, the behavior of the growth rate up to the O(1/k 2 ) term is controlled by powers whose tail is of length 1 or 2. It seems natural to wonder whether increasing the precision up to the O(1/k 3 ) term requires precisely the considerations of powers with tails of length 3. Shall the degree of the order of precision grow linearly with respect to the length of the tails?
context: As mentioned in the introduction (see Equation (3)), our result provides for all p a good estimate for α(k, p) up to an error term 1/k + O(1/k 2 ). When we only care about powers n isomorphic to 1 . . . ℓ1 and 12 . . . ℓ12, the difference between p-powers for p ≥ n−1 and for n p > n−1 lies only in the range of ℓ. By varying the length ℓ, we might allow ourselves to n address p-powers for a fraction p that may be of more complicated nature than n−1 . So  + n n applying our approach for all p instead of only p of the form n−1 or n−1 might be enough to replace this error term by O(1/k 2 ). On the other hand, as conjectured by Shur, and later by the second author, the behavior of the growth rate up to the O(1/k 2 ) term is controlled by powers whose tail is of length 1 or 2. It seems natural to wonder whether increasing the precision up to the O(1/k 3 ) term requires precisely the considerations of powers with tails of length 3.
